records.name: Lancaster Avenue 21st Century Business Association
records.summary: A community development group for the Lancaster Avenue corridor in West Philadelphia. It helps small businesses start and grow, and as a registered community organization it gives neighbors a place to hear about zoning and development projects and respond.
records.what_you_do: Business owners can use training, startup and growth programs and one-on-one office hours. Neighbors hear about zoning and development projects in the area and can respond through the group's community role.

schedule.text: Open office hours with one-on-one business guidance on the second Thursday of each month at 10 am, in person. Online office hours are also listed for 5:30 pm.

cost.text: Membership is billed yearly: $45 a year for non-business owners, $150 a year for business owners, and $500 a year for corporate sponsors. The site lists no prices for office hours or events.

first_step.how: Call 215-883-0109 or email la21info@la21philly.org and ask how neighbors can take part in the registered community organization.
first_step.basis: The site gives a phone number and an email, but it lists no neighbor meeting dates, and membership costs $45 a year or more, so the way in for neighbors is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: Most of what the group lists is business help: one-on-one office hours on the second Thursday of the month at 10 am, plus online office hours. The site does not describe a first visit for neighbors, so start with a call.
first_visit_tips: Call before you come, since the site lists no neighbor meeting dates or times.
The group lists two locations: 3500 Lancaster Avenue and 3675 Market Street.
If you decide to join, the non-business membership is $45 a year.

records.notes: Tier 1 email jwilliams@la21philly.org and phone 267-736-8163 came from the City RCO list. The group's own contact details (la21info@la21philly.org and 215-883-0109) replace them here. The site lists no RCO meeting dates, times or places, and the upcoming events page gives no years, so no event dates are written. Membership figures come from the membership page. Fetches used for this group: 4. Searches: 0.

records.name: Mt. Vernon Manor, Inc.
records.summary: A community development group in the Mantua area of West Philadelphia, formed in 1977. It runs a weekly food pantry, helps residents with rent, utility and property tax costs, and runs the neighborhood advisory committee that links residents to City services.
records.what_you_do: Sign in at the Wednesday 9 am food pantry, ask for help with rent, utilities, property taxes or benefits, or take part in the elected neighborhood subcommittee, which meets monthly to name local needs.

schedule.text: Food pantry every Wednesday at 9 am, with sign-in. The elected Neighborhood Advisory Subcommittee meets monthly, and the site gives no meeting time or place.

first_step.how: Call the office at 215-475-9492 on a weekday between 9 am and 3 pm and ask how to join the subcommittee or start with the Wednesday food pantry.
first_step.basis: The Wednesday pantry takes sign-ins, which is simple, but the site does not say how to join the elected subcommittee or whether its meetings are open to visitors.
first_step.what_to_expect: The pantry is a weekly sign-in on Wednesday mornings at 9 am. The site does not describe a subcommittee meeting, so ask the office about its time and place before you go.
first_visit_tips: Plan to sign in when you arrive at the Wednesday pantry.
Call first to confirm when and where the subcommittee meets.
The site lists office hours of weekdays 9 am to 3 pm.

records.notes: The homepage gives the pantry time and the weekday office hours. The contact page lists only a phone and an email and no hours, so the homepage is cited for hours. The site's general email is info@mvmcdc.org; the tier 1 email michael@mvmcdc.org (City NAC list) is kept, and the general address is worth using for first contact. The pantry address, cost and eligibility are not stated. The community partners page names no partners in its text (logos only), so no leads were logged. Fetches used for this group: 5. Searches: 0.

records.name: Ollin Yoliztli Calmecac
records.summary: A Philadelphia group founded in 2003 to explore and share Mexicayotl culture, a tradition from Mexico before the Spanish arrived. It runs events, a radio show and an Indigenous Peoples Day celebration.
records.what_you_do: Come to the group's festivals and celebrations, follow the Nika Tlaka radio show, or volunteer on the board, in marketing and social media, or in dancing and music. Donations are also welcome.

schedule.text: A few festivals and celebrations each year, including the Philadelphia Indigenous Peoples Day celebration. The site does not list dates for any of them.

cost.text: The site asks for donations. It shows no membership fees or event prices.

first_step.how: Email brujo@ollinyoliztlicalmecac.org to say you would like to volunteer, or ask about the next festival.
first_step.basis: The volunteer page names an email route with no application form, and the group holds public festivals. The site shows no dates or steps for a first visit.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a first visit. Volunteers are needed for board work, marketing and social media, and dancing or music, and most events are bilingual.
first_visit_tips: Email before you come, since the site shows no event dates or times.
If you dance or play music, say so in your email, because the group lists both as needs.

records.notes: The events page was blocked (403) in tier 1 and was not retried. The members page gives no join steps or fees, and the blog has no posts. Most events are bilingual according to the volunteer page, but the second language is not named, so no access.languages are written. A search result describes a 15th annual Indigenous Peoples Day celebration at Bartram's Garden on Sunday, October 12, 2025, co-hosted with this group, and a Bartram's Garden post is dated October 9, 2025. The fetched Bartram's page did not name the group in the text I read, so that lead is not used for status; a reviewer should check it before moving status to active. Fetches used for this group: 6 (cap). Searches: 1.

records.name: Philadelphia Archaeological Forum
records.summary: A group that shares Philadelphia's archaeology with the public and speaks up to protect historic sites. It hosts public talks, runs a historical burial grounds map and database, and invites people to join advocacy actions.
records.what_you_do: Attend public talks, sign petitions, and send public comments to the City Planning Commission during its reviews. Membership is open to anyone interested in archaeology, history or related fields.

schedule.text: Public talks and events, mostly in October during Pennsylvania Archaeology Month. The group's activities page lists a yearly public day, Explore Philly's Buried Past, held each October since 2005. Other talks are posted one at a time, and many need registration.

cost.text: Membership dues are $15 a calendar year. Some talks are free, and some ticketed talks charge admission.

first_step.how: Pick a public talk from the events list on the group's website and register for it if the listing asks you to.
first_step.basis: Public talks are open to anyone, and a general email is posted. Several talks need registration first, and membership is $15 a year.
first_step.what_to_expect: Talks cover Philadelphia's burial grounds, digs and historic sites, and are given by archaeologists and other specialists. Some are online, and the state historic preservation office's lunchtime lectures run about 20 minutes and end with questions.
first_visit_tips: Check each listing for registration, since several talks use Eventbrite.
Museum talks are ticketed through the museum's own site.
Membership forms are downloaded from the website and mailed with dues.

records.notes: The homepage shows 2026 for the October 2, October 16 and October 30 talks. A first read of the homepage also gave 2026 for the October 12 Indigenous Peoples Day event and the October 21 Penn Museum talk, but a second read showed no year for them, so those two are not written with a year. Membership is $15 a calendar year, paid by a mailed form. The contact page lists phillyarchaeology@gmail.com; the membership page says its email link points elsewhere, so confirm the address before publishing. Some talks are virtual, so online_ok is set to true. The tier 1 interest historic_site_volunteering was dropped because the site lists no volunteer roles. Named partners that are venues or government bodies (Penn Museum, National Constitution Center, I-95 Archaeology Center, Independence National Historical Park, State Historic Preservation Office) are not logged as leads. Fetches used for this group: 5. Searches: 0.

records.name: Philadelphia Folklore Project
records.summary: A nonprofit founded in 1987 that documents, presents and supports folk and traditional arts in the Philadelphia area. Its events page lists workshops and exhibits from 2026, but it shows no upcoming dates yet.
records.what_you_do: Join the mailing list to hear about exhibits, films, workshops and concerts when they are announced. The group also offers a few unpaid volunteer and intern roles, tailored to each person.

schedule.text: No regular weekly program is posted. Exhibits, films, workshops and talks are announced one at a time on the events page.

cost.text: The site lists no event prices and no membership dues.

first_step.how: Sign up for the mailing list on the group's website so you hear about the next exhibit, film or workshop.
first_step.basis: Events are announced to the mailing list, but volunteer roles are few and placed one at a time after a phone call, and the events page lists no upcoming dates.
first_step.what_to_expect: The events page lists no upcoming dates, so a first visit depends on the next announcement. Volunteer roles are unpaid, limited in number, and tailored to each person, so expect to talk with the group before you start.
first_visit_tips: Call 215-726-1106 before you plan to volunteer, since places are limited.
The volunteer page says fluency in languages other than English is especially welcome.
Check the events page for the next exhibit, film or workshop to see what the group offers.

records.notes: Tier 1 said the site listed no dated events. The events page, headed Past Events, lists items dated in 2026 (a postponed January 29 meet-up, a March 14 workshop, the March 31 to July 11 exhibit, and a June 25 workshop). No item is dated after October 8, 2026, so no upcoming events are written. Status moved from probably active to active on the June 2026 workshop. The news page's newest item is dated February 26, 2025. The Community Kitchens page sells boxed dinners as a fundraiser, so it is not a joinable program and is not used. No email address was found on the site. Venues and schools named on the events page (Asian Arts Initiative, Folk Arts-Cultural Treasures Charter School, Temple University Library, Free Library) are not logged as leads. records.name: Powelton Village Civic Association
records.summary: An all-volunteer group of Powelton Village residents that is also a Registered Community Organization, so developers talk with it about nearby zoning and building plans. It also organizes clean-ups and social events.
records.what_you_do: Members vote on the association's decisions and leadership. Neighbors review nearby building and zoning proposals and share the association's view with the City and developers. Volunteers also run clean-ups and social events and care for parks, playgrounds and sidewalks.

schedule.text: Membership meetings run 7 to 8:30 pm. Some are held by video and some in person at Metropolitan Baptist Church. Each date is posted on the group's website.

locations.label: Meeting place (in person, Metropolitan Baptist Church)

cost.text: The site lists no dollar amounts for membership. Donations are also accepted.

first_step.how: Fill out the online membership form on the group's membership page.
first_step.basis: Any Powelton Village resident, owner or renter, can join through an online form, and meeting dates are posted publicly. The site does not say whether non-members can attend meetings.
first_step.what_to_expect: The association reviews nearby building and zoning proposals, and its membership meetings run 7 to 8:30 pm. Some meetings are by video, and the link is sent by the neighborhood email list before each one.
first_visit_tips: Get on the neighborhood email list so you receive the video link before a virtual meeting.
For an in-person meeting, the church is at 3500 Baring Street.
Current residents who are members can vote on the association's decisions and leadership.

records.notes: The meeting-notes page says the association holds monthly membership meetings, but the dates it lists (October 19 and November 16, 2026, January 25, 2027, and a September 2021 entry) do not show a monthly pattern, so no monthly schedule is written. The website shows no email or phone number and points to an online contact form and a P.O. Box; the tier 1 email rco_notice@poweltonvillage.org and phone 610-308-5524 come from the City RCO list and are kept. The tier 1 meeting place read 'or, Via Zoom'; it is split into an in-person place and an online option. Fetches used for this group: 4. Searches: 0.

records.name: Southwest CDC
records.summary: A community development group serving Southwest Philadelphia since 1987. It offers housing counseling, job and workforce help, an after-school program and a summer camp, and it runs the Neighborhood Advisory Committee, which gives residents a say in local planning.
records.what_you_do: Get help with housing counseling, job and workforce services, or money coaching. Families can use the after-school program for students at John Patterson Elementary, and neighborhood children can join the summer camp. Residents can also take part in the Neighborhood Advisory Committee's planning work.

schedule.text: The Neighborhood Advisory Subcommittee meets on the second Tuesday of each month. The site gives no meeting time or place, so call to confirm.

access.notes: Housing counselors are bilingual in Spanish and English.

first_step.how: Call Lorraine Thomas at 215-729-3948 to ask how to volunteer.
first_step.basis: The volunteer page gives one contact and no steps. The subcommittee meets monthly, but the page gives no time, place or sign-up for it, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe what a first visit involves. The office is at 6328 Paschall Avenue, and the main office line is 215-729-0800, so a phone call is the best first step.
first_visit_tips: Call before you go, since the site does not list office hours.
Housing counselors are bilingual in Spanish and English, so ask for that if it helps.
The after-school program is for students at John Patterson Elementary, so call a program coordinator to ask whether it fits your child.

records.notes: Tier 1 email donna@southwestcdc.org and phone 215-729-7441 come from the City NAC list and are kept. The group's own pages give the main office line 215-729-0800 and the volunteer contact Lorraine Thomas, which are used in the first step. The after-school program serves students at John Patterson Elementary, not the general public. The summer camp is open to all neighborhood children, with no dates given. The news page's newest item is dated November 21, 2025, and the tier 1 last sign of life (2026-10) comes from the City NAC record, so it is kept. Headlines on the news page about other organizations are not partners and are not logged. Fetches used for this group: 6 (cap). Searches: 0.
